quirks: Marriage records for African Americans in Spalding County were kept in separate 'colored' volumes — vol. F (1903–1910) and vol. I (1923–1933) are 100% indexed on FamilySearch (imageGroups 007718973 and 007718976); search these specifically for Ogletree and Pearcy family marriages.

Statewide birth registration began 1919 (general compliance by 1928); statewide death registration began 1919 (general compliance by 1922). Children born before 1919 will have no state birth certificate — use the 1900/1910/1920 census, delayed birth affidavits (FS collection 3438747), and church records instead.

Death records for African Americans were often filed in separate indexes — if a death is not found in the main Georgia Deaths index (FS collections 1320969 / 1385727), check for a 'colored' sub-series or the Georgia Archives Virtual Vault (https://vault.georgiaarchives.org/digital/collection/gadeaths/).

The 1920 (imageGroup 004300135) and 1930 (imageGroup 004532000) census volumes for Spalding County are 0% name-indexed on FamilySearch and must be browsed image-by-image; the 1900 census (imageGroups 004120084_001 and 004120083_004) is 96–97% indexed and fully searchable.

Spalding County records begin 1852; no record loss from the 1874 or 1981 courthouse fires (all records survived, per Paul K. Graham, Georgia Courthouse Disasters). Court, land, and probate records from 1852 held by Clerk of Superior Court, 132 W. Solomon St., Griffin, GA 30223.

Neighboring counties — Butts, Clayton, Coweta, Fayette, Henry, Lamar, Meriwether, Pike — border Spalding; families near county lines may have generated records on both sides. Search all adjoining counties for children or siblings who may have settled nearby.

The Griffin Spalding Historical Society (633 Meriwether St., Griffin, GA; griffinhistory.com) holds local family history materials and newspaper files, including the Griffin Daily News, useful for obituaries and social notices that name children.
entry.guide_markdown:
## Locality Guide: Spalding County, Georgia (1900–1930)

**Jurisdiction formed:** 20 December 1851 from Fayette, Henry, and Pike Counties. County seat: Griffin. No record loss from courthouse fires of 1874 or 1981 — all records survived.

**Neighboring counties:** Butts, Clayton, Coweta, Fayette, Henry, Lamar, Meriwether, Pike.

### Vital Records
*(Source: [Georgia Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Georgia_Vital_Records); [Spalding County, Georgia Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spalding_County,_Georgia_Genealogy))*

| Type | Statewide Registration | General Compliance |
|------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Births | 1919 | 1928 |
| Deaths | 1919 | 1922 |
| Marriages | County-level from 1852; statewide 1952 | 1952 |

**Birth substitutes (pre-1919):** 1900, 1910, 1920 census; delayed birth affidavits (FS collection 3438747, indexed); church christening registers.

**Key birth/death collections on FamilySearch:**
- [Georgia, County Delayed Birth and Death Records, 1870–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3438747) — index & images
- [Georgia, Deaths, 1914–1927](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1320969) — index & images
- [Georgia, Deaths, 1928–1943](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1385727) — index & images
- Georgia Archives Virtual Vault death certificates (1919–1930): https://vault.georgiaarchives.org/digital/collection/gadeaths/

### Marriage Records
**African American researchers:** Spalding County kept separate 'colored' marriage volumes:
- **Vol. F (1903–1910), colored** — imageGroup 007718973 — **100% indexed** ✅
- **Vol. I (1923–1933), colored** — imageGroup 007718976 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. E (1898–1903): imageGroup 007718972 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. G (1910–1917): imageGroup 007718974 — **100% indexed** ✅
- Vol. H (1917–1923): imageGroup 007718975 — **100% indexed** ✅

Statewide collections: [Georgia County Marriages 1785–1950](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1927197) (index & images); [Georgia Marriages 1808–1967](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1674807) (index only).

### Census Records
- **1900** (imageGroups 004120084_001, 004120083_004): **96–97% indexed** ✅
- **1910**: search via FS record search (national collection, well indexed) ✅
- **1920** (imageGroup 004300135): **0% indexed — browse-only** ❌
- **1930** (imageGroup 004532000): **0% indexed — browse-only** ❌

For 1920 and 1930, use Ancestry.com or MyHeritage where both years are indexed for Spalding County.

### Probate Records
- [Georgia, Probate Records, 1742–1990](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1999178) — index & images
- Spalding probate records (1892–1946): imageGroup 005782189 — **full-text searchable, not name-indexed**
- Will records (1929–1965): imageGroup 005782181 — **full-text searchable, not name-indexed**

### Newspapers / Obituaries
- *Griffin Daily News* and other local papers: [Digital Library of Georgia](https://gahistoricnewspapers.galileo.usg.edu/) — free access; [GenealogyBank](https://www.genealogybank.com/gbnk/newspapers/explore/USA/Georgia/) ($); Newspapers.com via Ancestry ($)
- Obituaries can name all surviving children — high priority for this question.

### Local Repositories
- **Georgia Archives**, 5800 Jonesboro Rd, Morrow, GA 30260 — statewide holdings
- **Griffin Spalding Historical Society**, 633 Meriwether St, Griffin, GA — local newspapers, family histories
- **Spalding County Courthouse**, 132 W. Solomon St., Griffin — court, land, and probate records from 1852
- Clerk Superior Court holds divorce and court records from 1852.

### African American Resources
See: [African American Resources for Georgia](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/African_American_Resources_for_Georgia). Key note: vital records and sometimes cemetery records for African Americans were kept in separate files with separate indexes — always search 'colored' or 'African American' sub-series specifically.

entry.rationale: The 1920 census will show children still in the household 10-15 years into the marriage. The family may still be in Spalding County or may have already migrated to Chicago. Per loc_001, the 1920 Spalding County census volume (imageGroup 004300135) is 0% indexed on FamilySearch — browse-only; Ancestry has it indexed. Search Ancestry for Lewis Ogletree in both Georgia and Illinois to locate the household wherever the family resided in January 1920.

By 1930 the family is expected to be in Chicago. The 1930 census will list all children still in the household, with ages that help calculate birth years. Per loc_001, the Spalding County 1930 census is also 0% indexed on FamilySearch; search both Spalding County, GA (if migration was later than expected) and Cook County, IL on FamilySearch or Ancestry. The 1930 census is indexed on FamilySearch for Illinois.

The 1940 US census is free and fully indexed on FamilySearch. By 1940 most children would be teenagers or adults; older children may have their own households nearby. Searching for the Lewis Ogletree household AND each known child's household in Cook County in 1940 will capture children who had moved out but remained in Chicago. Children still at home will be listed with the parents.

The Social Security NUMIDENT (United States, Social Security Numerical Identification Files, 1936-2007; FS collection 5000016) lists every person who applied for a Social Security number. Children of Lewis and Mattie born roughly 1906-1930 would have applied for SS in their 20s-30s (1940s-1960s). The NUMIDENT entry gives: birth date, birth place, parents' names (on the SS-5 application), and often death date. This is the single most powerful national cross-check for identifying and confirming children. Also search the Social Security Death Index (FS collection 1202535) for death dates of known children.

World War II draft registration cards (FamilySearch collection 1880573, Georgia; national via Ancestry) cover men born between 1877 and 1897 (1st registration) and 1886-1897 and 1897-1927 (later registrations), capturing virtually all adult men in 1940. Sons of Lewis and Mattie born c.1906-1927 would appear. Each card lists: full name, birth date and place, employer, and next of kin — often the father or mother, confirming the Lewis Ogletree parentage link. Lewis Ogletree (L5D9-KXT already in tree) is a candidate son; his draft card, if found, will name his birth date and parents.

Children who died in Georgia before or shortly after migration will appear in Georgia death certificates. Search: (a) Georgia Deaths 1914-1927 (FS collection 1320969, indexed & images) and (b) Georgia Deaths 1928-1943 (FS collection 1385727, indexed & images). Per loc_001, death records for African Americans were often filed in separate indexes — search both the main index and any 'colored' sub-series. A Georgia death certificate gives: name, age/birth date, parents' names, cause of death, and place of burial — all useful for confirming parentage and birth year.

Georgia County Delayed Birth Records 1870-1960 (FS collection 3438747, index & images) capture affidavits filed by Georgians who needed a birth certificate but lacked one — common for African Americans born before statewide registration (1919). Each affidavit names the applicant's birth date and place, parents' names, and witnesses. Children of Lewis and Mattie born 1906-1919 are likely candidates for delayed birth filings. Also check Georgia Births and Christenings 1754-1960 (FS collection 1674802, index only) for any christening records. Per loc_001, no statewide birth registration existed before 1919 in Georgia.

Children who married in Spalding County before the family migrated to Chicago will appear in county marriage records. Per loc_001, African American marriage records in Spalding County were kept in separate 'colored' volumes: vol. F (1903-1910, imageGroup 007718973, 100% indexed), vol. G (1910-1917, imageGroup 007718974, 100% indexed), vol. H (1917-1923, imageGroup 007718975, 100% indexed), and vol. I (1923-1933, imageGroup 007718976, 100% indexed). Search for the surname Ogletree in all four volumes. Harriett Haygood (K45Y-CC5, already in tree) may have married a Haygood in this county — her marriage record would confirm parentage. Also search the statewide Georgia County Marriages 1785-1950 (FS collection 1927197).

Obituaries for Lewis Washington Ogletree and Mattie Pearcy Ogletree in Chicago newspapers are among the highest-value sources for this question: they characteristically name ALL surviving children with their cities of residence, and sometimes deceased children as well. Search Chicago Defender (the primary African American newspaper in Chicago, 1905-present) and Chicago Tribune via Newspapers.com / GenealogyBank / ProQuest on Ancestry and other platforms. A Cook County locality guide (not yet created) will identify the full suite of Illinois vital record collections; for now, this item targets newspaper obituaries and death notices as the most actionable external source. Note: Lewis and Mattie's Cook County death certificates (when found) will also name an informant — usually a child — and may list survivors.

Link this persona to L5D9-KXT despite the conflicting tree date; the 1914 identification is already established with 0.969 score.

Louise in this Chicago household is therefore NOT a confirmed child of Lewis Sr. and Mattie. She may be another sibling of Lewis Sr. or a more distant relative. Create a new stub person for Louise unless same_person scores above ~0.5 against an existing tree person.

4. **GW4W-DTG** is Lewis Washington Ogletree Sr. (subject, b. 1882 GA). He is the father of Lewis Jr. (L5D9-KXT) and Annie (I2) and Guyson (I3). Hattie is his SIBLING. Do not link any src_006 persona to GW4W-DTG.

5. **GJZY-622** is Nellie Mae Ogletree (pre-existing in tree). Not relevant to this household.

5. For Lewis W Ogletree (lodger): link to L5D9-KXT
6. For Louise Ogletree (lodger): score against existing persons; if no match above ~0.4, create a new stub (call it something like "Louise Ogletree, b.~1908 GA, lodger in Hattie Ogletree household, Chicago 1930")

Use `research_append` with section "person_evidence" to write each pe_ entry. Write the rationale for each link including same_person score. Include any relevant notes about confidence and what further research would upgrade or downgrade the link.

args.prompt:
Write a GPS-conformant proof conclusion for question q_001 in the Ogletree children research project.

**Project path:** `C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\e2e-ogletree-children-3y4cy2ic`
**Question ID:** q_001 — "Who were all the children born to Lewis Washington Ogletree (b. 1882, Georgia) and his wife Mattie Pearcy (m. 1905, Spalding County, Georgia)?"

**Summary of evidence (read full assertions from research.json for details):**

CONFIRMED CHILDREN (multiple independent corroborating sources):
1. **Annie Ogletree (I2, b.~1908-1909 GA):** Named as daughter in the 1910 Spalding County census (src_001, a_001-a_035, head=L W Ogletree, wife=Mattie). The 1920 Spalding County marriage record (src_003) confirms "Annie L Ogletree" married Willie C Berry — same person.
2. **Guyson Ogletree (I3, b.~1909-1910 GA):** Named as son in the 1910 Spalding County census (src_001). No subsequent record corroborated, but household position and age are consistent.
3. **Lewis Washington Ogletree Jr. (L5D9-KXT, b. 16 Apr 1914 Griffin, Spalding County, GA):** WWII draft card (src_005, ark:/61903/1:1:QPZW-ZVNT, original image confirmed) gives full name, birth date 16 Apr 1914, birthplace Griffin GA. Same person found in 1930 Chicago census (src_006, lodging in aunt Hattie's household) and 1940 Chicago census (src_007). The 1905 Lewis-Mattie marriage and 1914 birth are consistent. No direct statement of parentage in a single source (no birth certificate), but four independent sources converge on identity.

POSSIBLE CHILDREN (unconfirmed parentage, further research needed):
4. **Girard Ogletree (I8, b.~1912 GA):** Found in 1930 Chicago census (src_008) as a lodger in Hattie Ogletree's household alongside other Ogletrees. Ogletree surname, Georgia birth, Chicago residence consistent with the family network. No record states parentage.
5. **Willie M Ogletree (I9, b.~1913 GA, female):** Same household as Girard (src_008, 1930 Chicago). Same analysis applies.

NOT CHILDREN (ruled out):
- Hattie Ogletree (I5): Lewis Sr.'s SIBLING — WWII draft card image (Field 8 = "AUNT") is a primary source confirming she is Lewis Jr.'s aunt, not his mother or sister.
- Louise Ogletree (I6): Death certificate (parents Sun Smoot / Julia Ogletree) documents a different family line.
- Samuel, Osduines, James E, Keattie, Walker Ogletree (I16-I20): Lewis Sr.'s siblings from 1900 family-of-origin census (src_010).

**Known evidentiary gaps:**
- Spalding County GA 1920 and 1930 census volumes are 0%-indexed on FamilySearch (browse-only) — the family could not be name-searched in these years; this limits corroboration for children born ~1910-1920
- No birth certificates found for any child (Georgia didn't require statewide birth registration until 1919, with erratic coverage in rural areas through the 1920s)
- The 1930 L W Ogletree / Ada Morris marriage (src_004, Spalding County) creates some ambiguity about Lewis Sr.'s situation in 1930, but does not affect the child-identification findings
- Lewis Jr.'s erroneous 1856 birth fact in the tree is a known data error from a bad FamilySearch merge, not a true conflict — the correct date (16 Apr 1914) is established by the WWII draft card at 0.969 same_person score

**GPS tier assessment:**
- Annie and Guyson: **Proved** — 1910 census is an original record directly naming them as children of L W and Mattie in Spalding County. For Annie: the 1920 marriage record adds independent corroboration.
- Lewis Jr.: **Proved** (or Probable) — indirect convergence from four sources (1905 marriage establishes parents; 1914 birth in Griffin GA; 1930/1940 Chicago censuses; WWII draft card) with no contradicting evidence.
- Overall answer tier: **Probable** given the inability to name-search the 1920/1930 Spalding censuses and the possible existence of additional unconfirmed children (Girard, Willie M).

**Instructions:**
1. Read research.json assertions and person_evidence for q_001 context (research_query)
2. Select the appropriate GPS proof tier and form
3. Write a self-contained proof summary narrative covering:
   - The confirmed children and their evidentiary basis
   - The possible children and why they are unconfirmed
   - The ruled-out individuals and why
   - The known evidentiary gaps
4. Persist the proof_summaries entry via research_append
5. If exhaustive_declaration for q_001 has not yet been written (check questions[] status), leave q_001 open rather than marking it resolved — the exhaustiveness agent is running in parallel
6. Encode the conclusions in tree.gedcomx.json at the appropriate GPS tier

If the assertion or its log entry cannot be resolved at all, say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver.
